verdict_summary: Every load-bearing SCHEDULE conclusion survives independent re-derivation from the saved bytes and from live/archive re-fetches performed today. The encodable output - five keys, five launch days, four distinct closes, two order-entry revision rows, the withheld 16:00-16:15 Sunday quarter-hour, and the Closed (not Maintenance) inter-trade-date gaps - is unchanged by this review. matches=false is returned for two evidence-discipline defects in the result document itself (a fabricated product code inside a `verbatim` field, and a load-bearing citation with no evidence row) plus two overstated-scope claims. All four are correctable by editing the result JSON; none moves a boundary.

discrepancies.claim: "The complete \"CME Globex Contracts\" TAS list is CLT, BZT, BBT, HOT, NGT, RBT, RET."
discrepancies.finding: False, and partly fabricated. Re-extracted rul083109nymexandcomex001.pdf (sha256 a5693b21c1e57d54b043968a5066afee3556d5758c047435fcfc59a10e2111f1, matches) with pdftotext -layout; my render is byte-identical to the researcher's own rul083109nymexandcomex001.txt. The document's complete CME Globex Contracts TAS list is ELEVEN codes: WST, RTI, BHT, HPT, HHT, BBT, CLT, HOT, NGT, RBT, RET. The string "BZT" occurs ZERO times in the document (grep -c "BZT" = 0; the full set of three-letter uppercase tokens in the file is BBT BHT CLT CME COM HHT HOT HPT MOC NGT RBT RET RTI SEP TAS THE WST WTI). BZT first appears in the NEXT advisory (RA1002-4, 2010-02-02), where it is correctly quoted. So five real codes were dropped and one was imported from a different document - i.e. this `verbatim` was written from memory, which the gate brief forbids.
discrepancies.impact: The conclusion this state carries - that RA0907-4's complete TAS list contains no gold, no silver and no copper - is TRUE and I verified it independently. The floor negative stands. But the defect is the exact failure mode this gate exists to catch, and it removes the presumption that the result's other quotes were byte-derived. I re-checked every other quote in the result myself (see verified_independently) and they hold.
discrepancies.fix: Replace the sentence with the eleven actual codes, or drop the enumeration and keep only the load-bearing negative.

discrepancies.claim: "the 16:48/16:49/16:50 cells on the 2012-06-16 hours page are a stale page, not a live state."
discrepancies.finding: As submitted this is an assertion against a LATER-dated observation (capture 2012-06-16) using an EARLIER-dated notice (2012-04-09), with nothing in the result's evidence set showing the page ever adopting the notice's values before 2015-03-22. That is the shape AGENTS.md handles as a source conflict ('serve what both state, withhold only what they dispute, and record the conflict beside the table'), not by declaring one side stale. The reading is nevertheless CORRECT, and I proved it from two captures in the very channel the researcher had already indexed but did not fetch: web.archive.org/web/20120914235904id_/ and /20130902013752id_/ of http://www.cmegroup.com/trading_hours/metals-hours.html both print, for Gold TAS, Silver TAS and Copper TAS alike, 'Pre-Open Electronic Trading (Weekday) 17:45-17:46 ET (16:45-16:46 CT)' - the 2012-04-09 notice's uniform randomised minute. Saved as mh-20120914235904.html (sha256 c7937f9bcd34926598a5a62052ebebd35a496df8e9006b8927ed2a1bab710c78) and mh-20130902013752.html (761e2c2ebfa8bc09d803987f8cbf8c54aa2abea201d129abb45dc4a905075460).
discrepancies.impact: Order-entry only; no executable boundary. With these two captures the staleness reading is evidenced rather than asserted and the conflict disappears.
discrepancies.fix: Add the 2012-09-14 and 2013-09-02 captures as a state and restate correction 6 as an evidenced bracket: the hours page shows 16:48/16:49/16:50 at 2012-06-16 and 16:45-16:46 at 2012-09-14, so the 2012-06-16 weekday cell lagged the 2012-04-15 change by under three months.

discrepancies.where: states[11] ('CME metals trading-hours page, four archived captures') and its bears_on ('across 3.5 years of this channel')

discrepancies.finding: The CDX for cmegroup.com/trading_hours/metals-hours.html (fetched today, saved as cdxmh.json, sha256 2f14c77eddde9432f0572c51b4480e63b696e7b8571969ebc8e3735bdaade83d) returns 29 distinct-digest 200-status captures from 2009-05-01 to 2015-03-22, then only 301s (2015-09-06 onward). Four of 29 were examined. I fetched six more as an adversarial probe. Result: the claim SURVIVES and is strengthened. (a) 2010-03-30 and 2010-04-30 - the latter nineteen days after the gold/silver TAS launch - contain NO TAS rows at all, so no direct launch-era observation was missed and the carry-back from RA1006-4 is not superseded by an available source. (b) 2012-09-14, 2013-09-02, 2014-07-07 and 2014-11-04 all print the same executable window for all three metals: 18:00-13:30 / 18:00-13:25 / 18:00-13:00 ET (17:00-12:30 / 12:25 / 12:00 CT). So 'the executable window never moves' now rests on eight samples, not four, spanning 2011-10-29 to 2015-03-22 with no gap wider than a year.
discrepancies.impact: None to the conclusion. The wording should say the channel was sampled at N points and that its last 200-status capture is 2015-03-22, not imply exhaustion at four.
discrepancies.fix: State the channel bound (last 200 capture 2015-03-22; 301 thereafter) and the sample count. Optionally fold in the six captures above.

residual_caveats: OBSERVATION GAP, gold/silver/copper close, 2015-03-22 -> 2019-11-18. Real and correctly reasoned, and now bounded as a CHANNEL EXHAUSTION rather than a sampling choice: metals-hours.html has no 200-status capture after 2015-03-22, and the contract-specification channel carried no TAS hours line until autumn 2019 (verified: gold spec 2019-09-24 has no TAS hours line, 2019-11-18 does; copper 2019-07-20 none, 2019-12-20 present). The 2015-09-20 non-move therefore rests on (a) the 2015-08-17 notice's own scope - it moves closes that sat at 16:15 CT to 16:00 CT, and metals TAS closed at 12:30/12:25/12:00 CT - and (b) identical values on either side of the gap. Both hold. Record the gap beside the rows.

OBSERVATION GAP, platinum 2021-04-11 -> 2026-03-10 and palladium 2021-05-13 -> 2026-05-27. I independently re-ran the CDX: productId 445 has exactly ONE 200-status capture (20260527221952) and 446 exactly two sharing one digest (20260310171835, 20260410064201). RA1005-4 zone-label argument (CORRECTIONS item 5) is an inference, not a statement, and is presented with more force than 'confirmation' usually carries. It is well supported: RA1006-4 shifts EVERY row of the same table by exactly +1h (CLT 1:30->2:30, 7FT 11:00->12:00, KTT 11:30->12:30, CJT 10:50->11:50, TTT 1:15->2:15, YOT 11:30->12:30, GCT 12:30->1:30, SIT 12:25->1:25, shared end 4:45->5:45) while relabelling the column from 'Globex Pre-Open Time Period' to 'No-Activity Period' - a uniform whole-hour shift of eight unrelated products is far better explained by a CT/ET relabel than by eight simultaneous substantive changes. Note the alternative reading that RA1005-4's column genuinely was an order-entry window and RA1006-4 replaced it with its complement; under either reading RA1005-4 contributes no session boundary and the encodable window comes from RA1006-4, so nothing turns on it.
